elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: Inserted cap: "may, no more than once per year and upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice". A once-per-year cap substantively limits frequency, though "per year" is undefined and could be read as a calendar year rather than a rolling 12-month window (preferred wording would be "once in any twelve (12) month period").

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Retained existing language: "upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company".
Retained: inspection "during the Company's normal business hours".

elements.element: Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: The right is exercisable by "HDI's General Manager" — the Vendor's own officer, not an independent third-party auditor; the redline does not change the identity of the inspecting person.

elements.element: The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: Section 3.4 as rendered contains no confidentiality undertaking for the inspecting person. The rationale points to a general § 8.3 confidentiality obligation on HDI, but that text is not before us and cannot be confirmed to cover records reviewed on inspection.

elements.element: Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
elements.evidence: No off-site preference appears anywhere in the rendered clause; inspection of "the records of the Company's General Manager" during Company business hours contemplates on-site review.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Retained: "The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI." Vendor bears its inspection costs unconditionally, which is better than the 5% shift-back carve-out.

elements.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
elements.evidence: Condition does not arise: the right is confined to inspecting "the records of the Company's General Manager reasonably related to the calculation of such payments"; no clause grants access to, or remote connection with, Customer systems, so there was nothing to delete.

elements.element: Vendor may audit no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: Operative insertion: "may, no more than once per year and upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice" — matches the fallback frequency cap verbatim and cures the previously unlimited right.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 15 days' notice of an audit.
elements.evidence: Existing "no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company" exceeds the 15-day fallback minimum and is left unchanged.

elements.element: Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent.
elements.evidence: "The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI" — unconditional Vendor cost bearing, more favourable than the 10% carve-out; correctly left unchanged.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the single insertion "no more than once per year" supplies the missing frequency cap, and the pre-existing 30-day written notice and unconditional HDI-borne inspection fees already meet or better the other two fallback elements. The finding is correctly classified as a deviation (the unrestricted frequency was walk-away territory) and the redline resolves it.

Preferred level is not reached, and the drafter has not claimed it. To press preferred, the operative text would need: (a) substitution of "an independent certified public accountant selected by HDI and reasonably acceptable to the Company" for "HDI's General Manager"; (b) an express undertaking that the auditor execute or be bound by confidentiality obligations no less protective than § 8 before access; (c) an off-site-where-possible sentence (e.g. "such inspection shall be conducted remotely from copies provided by the Company where practicable"); and (d) tightening "once per year" to "once in any twelve (12) month period".

No system-access defect exists: the right is limited to records reasonably related to the payment calculation, so the redline guidance to delete system-access language is inapplicable and nothing was over-deleted.

Minimality holds — only the frequency words were added, favourable existing terms (30 days' notice, business hours, HDI-borne fees, records-only scope) are untouched, no operative term is duplicated, and no obligation outside the AUDIT checklist is introduced.

Intent is preserved: the inspection subject matter, timing constraint, business-hours limitation and cost allocation all survive without contradiction; the inserted cap reads grammatically as a qualification on the grant of the inspection right.

Drafting nit worth noting to the drafter (not a defect that fails the level): "per year" is undefined in the clause; if the Agreement elsewhere defines a contract or calendar year, consider aligning, otherwise a rolling twelve-month formulation avoids back-to-back December/January inspections.
Margin comment is accurate and consistent with the operative change — it states the cap added and confirms notice and cost terms were left as-is.
